title: Denethor II
blurb: Denethor was the proud Steward of Gondor and father of Boromir and Faramir. Despair drove him to burn himself during the siege of Minas Tirith.
book:
Denethor was the son of Ecthelion II and became Steward of Gondor in T.A. 2984. He married Finduilas of Dol Amroth, who died young. They had two sons, Boromir and Faramir.

Denethor was wise and stern. He guarded the city well and kept watch on Mordor through the palantír of Minas Tirith. Sauron used that stone to feed him despair. He grew to favour Boromir and to resent Gandalf and, in time, Faramir.

When Boromir died, Denethor was filled with grief. During the siege of T.A. 3019 he gave up all hope. He had the wounded Faramir carried to Rath Dínen to burn with him. Pippin, who had sworn service to him, fetched Gandalf, and Beregond stopped the servants.

Denethor refused to listen. He laid himself on a pyre in the House of the Stewards with the palantír in his hands and was burned on 15 March T.A. 3019. His line then yielded the city to King Elessar.
film: John Noble plays Denethor. The film makes him colder to Faramir and has him send Faramir on a hopeless ride to retake Osgiliath. He runs from the pyre in flames and leaps from the Citadel.

places.note: Rules Gondor from the Citadel as Steward from T.A. 2984 until his death.
Looks into the palantír in a hidden chamber of the White Tower.
Burns himself on a pyre in the House of the Stewards in T.A. 3019.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book V
The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A

title: Faramir
kind: Captain of Gondor, Prince of Ithilien
blurb: Faramir was the younger son of Denethor and a wise Captain of Gondor. He let Frodo and Sam go free and later married Éowyn.
book:
Faramir was born in T.A. 2983, the younger brother of Boromir. He was gentle, learned and loyal, and Gandalf valued his counsel. Denethor loved him less than Boromir.

As Captain of the rangers of Ithilien, Faramir led raids against Sauron's servants. In March T.A. 3019 his men captured Frodo and Sam and took them to Henneth Annûn. He learned of the Ring but refused to take it, though Boromir had wished to. He sent the hobbits on their way.

Faramir then fought in the retreat from Osgiliath and was struck down by a poisoned dart. Denethor believed him dying and tried to burn him alive. Beregond and Gandalf saved him, and Aragorn healed him in the Houses of Healing.

Faramir fell in love with Éowyn there. After the war Aragorn named him Prince of Ithilien, and he became the last Ruling Steward. He and Éowyn settled at Emyn Arnen.
film: David Wenham plays Faramir. The film shows him taking Frodo and Sam to Osgiliath and nearly giving up the Ring, before he changes his mind.

facts.Title: Prince of Ithilien, Steward of Gondor

places.note: Brings Frodo and Sam to the hidden cave and decides to let them go.
Fights in the retreat from Osgiliath and is struck down by a dart.
Is carried to the House of the Stewards, where Denethor tries to burn him.
Is healed by Aragorn and meets Éowyn.
Settles with Éowyn at Emyn Arnen after the war.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book IV
The Lord of the Rings, Book V
The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A

title: Beregond
kind: Guard of the Citadel of Gondor
blurb: Beregond was a soldier of the Citadel guard who befriended Pippin. He broke the law to save Faramir from Denethor's pyre.
book:
Beregond was a Man of Gondor, son of Baranor, and a guard of the Citadel in Minas Tirith. He met Pippin in the Citadel in T.A. 3019 and became his friend and guide.

His son Bergil also befriended the hobbit. When Denethor tried to burn Faramir, Beregond left his post. He slew the porter of the Closed Door and fought Denethor's servants at the House of the Stewards. He did this to save Faramir's life.

After the war Aragorn judged him. The king pardoned him because he had saved Faramir, but sent him out of the city for shedding blood in the Hallows. He then made Beregond Captain of the White Company, the guard of Faramir in Emyn Arnen.
film: Beregond does not appear in the films. Gandalf and Pippin save Faramir from the pyre instead.

places.note: Serves in the guard of the Citadel and befriends Pippin.
Fights Denethor's servants at the House of the Stewards to save Faramir.
Serves Faramir in Emyn Arnen as Captain of the White Company.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book V
The Lord of the Rings, Book VI

title: Bergil
blurb: Bergil was the young son of Beregond. He befriended Pippin and showed him around Minas Tirith during the days before the siege.
book:
Bergil was the young son of Beregond, a guard of the Citadel of Gondor. In T.A. 3019 the boy met Pippin, who was newly come to Minas Tirith.

Bergil took the hobbit through the city and spoke with him about Gondor and the war. Together they watched the companies of the outlands march in through the gate. They became friends.

Bergil is a minor figure. The books tell little of his later life.

places.note: Lives in the city and befriends Pippin in T.A. 3019.
Watches with Pippin as the companies of the outlands enter the city.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book V

title: Imrahil
blurb: Imrahil was the Prince of Dol Amroth, uncle of Boromir and Faramir. He was a brave captain at the Pelennor and the Black Gate.
book:
Imrahil ruled Dol Amroth in Belfalas. He was brother of Finduilas, so he was uncle to Boromir and Faramir. His house was said to carry Elvish blood from ancient times.

When Mordor attacked in T.A. 3019, he led the Knights of Dol Amroth to Minas Tirith. In a sortie before the siege he carried the wounded Faramir back to the city. After Denethor died, he held command in the city with Gandalf.

He fought in the Battle of the Pelennor Fields. After the battle he saw that Éowyn still lived and had her taken to the Houses of Healing. He was later among the Captains at the Black Gate.

Imrahil's daughter Lothíriel later married Éomer. He remained Prince of Dol Amroth under King Elessar.
film: Imrahil does not appear in the films.

places.note: Rules the principality from his seat at Dol Amroth.
Brings his knights to the city and holds command there after Denethor dies.
Leads the knights of Dol Amroth in the battle.
Marches to the Black Gate with the Captains of the West.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book V
The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A

title: Ioreth
kind: Old wise-woman of the Houses of Healing
blurb: Ioreth was an old woman who served in the Houses of Healing. She remembered the old saying that the hands of the king are hands of a healer.
book:
Ioreth was a wise-woman who worked in the Houses of Healing in Minas Tirith during the war of T.A. 3019. She was old and talkative.

After the siege, the wounded lay in the Houses and could not be cured by the usual art. Ioreth repeated an old saying of Gondor that the hands of the king are the hands of a healer. In this way the true king could be known.

Gandalf heard this and called for Aragorn. Aragorn healed Faramir, Éowyn and Merry with the herb athelas. Ioreth was among those who saw the king's healing.
film: Ioreth does not appear in the films.

places.note: Serves among the healers and recalls the saying that proves the king by his hands.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book V

title: Húrin of the Keys
kind: Warden of the Keys of Minas Tirith
blurb: Húrin held the office of Warden of the Keys of Minas Tirith during the War of the Ring in T.A. 3019.
book:
Húrin was a Man of Gondor and the Warden of the Keys of Minas Tirith in the time of the War of the Ring. His office gave him charge of the keys of the city.

When Aragorn came to be crowned in T.A. 3019, Húrin went out with Faramir and other captains of Gondor to meet him before the gate. The books tell little else of his deeds.
film: Húrin of the Keys does not appear in the films.

places.note: Holds the office of Warden of the Keys of the city in T.A. 3019.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book V

title: Mablung of Ithilien
blurb: Mablung was a ranger of Ithilien who served Faramir. He was with the company that met Frodo and Sam in T.A. 3019.
book:
Mablung was a Man of Gondor and one of the rangers of Ithilien. These rangers held the land between Gondor and Mordor in secret, under the command of Faramir.

In March T.A. 3019 he was in Faramir's company when it ambushed a force of Haradrim near the road. The company also met Frodo and Sam and brought them to the hidden refuge of Henneth Annûn.

Mablung and the other rangers watched the land closely and kept the hobbits under guard until Faramir decided to let them go.

places.note: Serves in Faramir's company at the hidden cave of Henneth Annûn.
Joins the ambush of the Haradrim on the road in North Ithilien.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book IV

title: Damrod
blurb: Damrod was a ranger of Ithilien who served Faramir. He helped guard Frodo and Sam in T.A. 3019.
book:
Damrod was a Man of Gondor and a ranger of Ithilien. He served under Faramir, with his comrade Mablung.

In March T.A. 3019 the rangers ambushed the Haradrim and then met Frodo and Sam. Damrod helped to guard the two hobbits and took part in the march to Henneth Annûn.

The books give him only a small part in the tale.

places.note: Serves in Faramir's company at the hidden cave of Henneth Annûn.
Joins the ambush of the Haradrim on the road in North Ithilien.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book IV

title: Forlong the Fat
blurb: Forlong was the Lord of Lossarnach. He led his people to Minas Tirith and fell in the Battle of the Pelennor Fields.
book:
Forlong was the Lord of Lossarnach, a land of green valleys south of Minas Tirith. He was old and stout, but he was a loyal servant of Gondor.

When the Steward called for aid in T.A. 3019, Forlong came to Minas Tirith with a host of his people. The men of Lossarnach marched with axes in their hands.

Forlong fought in the Battle of the Pelennor Fields. Enemies surrounded him, and he was slain there.
film: Forlong does not appear in the films.

places.note: Rules Lossarnach as its lord.
Leads his men to the battle and is slain on the Pelennor Fields.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book V

title: Angbor the Fearless
blurb: Angbor was the Lord of Lamedon. He alone stood his ground at Linhir when the Dead came, and then followed Aragorn to the war.
book:
Angbor was the Lord of Lamedon, a land in the south-west of Gondor. In T.A. 3019 his men fought the Corsairs and the Haradrim at the fords of Linhir on the Gilrain.

When Aragorn came with the Army of the Dead, both sides fled in terror. Only Angbor stayed to meet him. Aragorn bade him gather his people and follow to the war.

Angbor later led the men of Lamedon to Minas Tirith.
film: Angbor does not appear in the films.

places.note: Fights at the fords of Linhir and alone stands to meet Aragorn there.
Rules Lamedon as its lord.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book V

title: Ecthelion II
blurb: Ecthelion II was the Steward of Gondor before Denethor. He trusted Gandalf and Thorongil, who was Aragorn in disguise.
book:
Ecthelion II was the twenty-fifth Ruling Steward of Gondor and the father of Denethor. He ruled from T.A. 2953 to 2984 and was a wise lord.

He gathered men of worth into his service. Among them was a captain named Thorongil, who was Aragorn in disguise. Thorongil often urged Ecthelion to trust Gandalf rather than Saruman. Denethor was jealous of Thorongil's place in his father's favour.

Ecthelion died in T.A. 2984. His son Denethor then became Steward.
film: Ecthelion II does not appear in the films.

places.note: Rules Gondor from Minas Tirith and takes Thorongil into his service.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A
The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B

title: Mardil Voronwë
blurb: Mardil Voronwë served King Eärnur and became the first Ruling Steward of Gondor after the king vanished.
book:
Mardil Voronwë was the Steward of King Eärnur. His surname means the Steadfast.

When Eärnur rode to Minas Morgul in T.A. 2050 and did not return, Mardil took charge of Gondor. He ruled in the name of the king. His house became the line of the Ruling Stewards, who held the land until the return of the king.

Mardil ruled for thirty years and died in T.A. 2080. The Stewards who came after him ruled for almost a thousand years.
film: Mardil does not appear in the films.

places.note: Rules Gondor from Minas Tirith after the loss of King Eärnur.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A
The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B

title: Cirion
blurb: Cirion was the Steward who gave the land of Calenardhon to Eorl the Young, founding the realm of Rohan.
book:
Cirion was the twelfth Ruling Steward of Gondor. He ruled from T.A. 2489 until T.A. 2567.

In T.A. 2510 Orcs and Easterlings attacked Gondor, and the northern army was cut off. Eorl the Young and the Éothéod rode to the Field of Celebrant and saved it.

As a reward, Cirion gave Eorl the land of Calenardhon. The two men swore an oath of friendship, and the oath was sworn upon the Halifirien. Calenardhon became Rohan.
film: Cirion does not appear in the films.

places.note: Leads Gondor's army at the Field of Celebrant, where Eorl rides to its aid.
Swears the oath with Eorl on the hill of Halifirien.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A
Unfinished Tales

title: Eärnur
blurb: Eärnur was the last King of Gondor. He rode to Minas Morgul to answer the Witch-king's challenge and was never seen again.
book:
Eärnur was the son of Eärnil II and the last king of Gondor. He was a bold warrior who loved arms more than counsel.

After Angmar overran Arthedain in T.A. 1974, he led a fleet from Gondor to Lindon. He commanded the cavalry at the Battle of Fornost. When the Witch-king rode against him, Eärnur's horse bolted, and the Witch-king escaped.

Eärnur became king in T.A. 2043. The Witch-king then challenged him to single combat. Mardil held him back the first time. In T.A. 2050 a second challenge came, and Eärnur rode to Minas Morgul with a few knights. He was never seen again and left no heir.

His Steward Mardil took charge, and the line of Ruling Stewards began.
film: Eärnur does not appear in the films.

places.note: Lands at the Grey Havens with the fleet of Gondor to aid Arnor.
Leads the cavalry in the defeat of Angmar in T.A. 1975.
Rules Gondor from Minas Tirith from T.A. 2043.
Rides into Minas Morgul in T.A. 2050 and is never seen again.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A

title: Eärnil II
kind: King of Gondor and victor of the Camp
blurb: Eärnil II was a captain who became King of Gondor. He defeated the Wainriders and Haradrim in T.A. 1944.
book:
Eärnil II was a captain of Gondor's southern army and a descendant of King Telumehtar. In T.A. 1944 the Wainriders destroyed the northern army and killed King Ondoher.

Eärnil defeated the Haradrim in South Ithilien. He then came north and destroyed the Wainriders' camp in the Battle of the Camp.

In T.A. 1945 the crown was given to Eärnil, and Arvedui's claim was set aside. Eärnil later sent his son Eärnur with a fleet to help Arvedui against Angmar, but it came too late to save Arthedain. Eärnil died in T.A. 2043, and Eärnur took the crown.
film: Eärnil II does not appear in the films.

places.note: Defeats the army of the Haradrim in South Ithilien in T.A. 1944.
Destroys the camp of the Wainriders and wins the battle.
Rules Gondor as king from T.A. 1945 until his death.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A

title: Castamir the Usurper
blurb: Castamir was the Admiral of Gondor who took the crown from King Eldacar in the Kin-strife. Eldacar slew him at the Crossings of Erui.
book:
Castamir was the captain of the fleet of Gondor. He was a descendant of the royal house and led the rebels in the Kin-strife, a civil war over the crown.

In T.A. 1437 his forces burned Osgiliath and drove out King Eldacar, who had mixed Northman blood. Castamir took the throne but ruled cruelly.

Eldacar returned with an army. In T.A. 1447 the two met at the Crossings of Erui, and Eldacar killed Castamir. His sons and followers fled to Umbar and became the Corsairs.
film: Castamir does not appear in the films.

places.note: Leads the rebels who burn Osgiliath and force out King Eldacar.
Is slain in the battle at the Crossings of Erui in T.A. 1447.

offmap.name: Umbar
offmap.note: His sons and followers settle there and become the Corsairs.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A

title: Telumehtar Umbardacil
kind: King of Gondor, conqueror of Umbar
blurb: Telumehtar Umbardacil was the King of Gondor who captured Umbar from the Corsairs in T.A. 1810.
book:
Telumehtar was a king of Gondor. His family had long suffered from the Corsairs, the descendants of Castamir's followers.

In T.A. 1810 Telumehtar sailed against Umbar and took the city. He slew the last lords of the house of Castamir in the fighting. He then added Umbardacil to his name, meaning conqueror of Umbar.

Umbar remained in Gondor's hands for a long time after that. It was later lost again.
film: Telumehtar does not appear in the films.

places.note: Rules Gondor from Minas Anor, the royal seat since T.A. 1640.

offmap.name: Umbar
offmap.note: Captures the stronghold of the Corsairs in T.A. 1810.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A

title: Witch-king of Angmar
kind: Lord of the Nazgûl, Lord of Angmar
blurb: The Witch-king was the chief of the Nazgûl and ruler of Angmar. He destroyed Arnor, stabbed Frodo, and died at the Pelennor.
book:
The Witch-king was a Man who took one of the Nine Rings and became the chief of the Nazgûl. About T.A. 1300 he came north and founded the realm of Angmar.

He destroyed the kingdom of Arnor in long wars against its successors. In T.A. 1974 he took Fornost, but Elves from Lindon and Gondorian forces drove him from the north. He fled to Mordor and gathered the other Nazgûl.

In T.A. 2002 the Nine took Minas Ithil. It became Minas Morgul. In T.A. 2050 King Eärnur accepted his challenge and rode into Minas Morgul. Eärnur was never seen again.

In T.A. 3018 he led the Nazgûl against Frodo at Weathertop. At the siege of Minas Tirith he broke the gates. On the Pelennor, Éowyn and Merry slew him, as an old prophecy said no man could.
film: The films show him mostly as a black rider and on a winged beast. In the extended edition of the third film he confronts Gandalf in the city and breaks his staff. The films do not show his history in Angmar.

places.note: Rules the realm of Angmar from Carn Dûm from about T.A. 1300.
Takes Fornost in T.A. 1974 and is defeated there in 1975.
Takes Minas Ithil with the Nazgûl in T.A. 2002.
Holds Minas Morgul as his fortress from T.A. 2002.
Stabs Frodo with a Morgul-blade on Weathertop.
Is slain by Éowyn and Merry on the Pelennor Fields.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book V
The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A
Unfinished Tales

title: Gothmog of Minas Morgul
blurb: Gothmog was the lieutenant of Minas Morgul. He led Mordor's host on the Pelennor after the fall of the Witch-king.
book:
Gothmog was a servant of Sauron and a lieutenant of the tower of Minas Morgul. He served the Witch-king of Angmar.

When the Witch-king fell in T.A. 3019, Gothmog took command of Mordor's army on the Pelennor. He drove the host onward against the defenders of Minas Tirith.

The books say little of his fate. He should not be confused with Gothmog, the Lord of Balrogs in the First Age.
film: The films show Gothmog as a deformed Orc commander who leads the siege forces. Lawrence Makoare plays him.

places.note: Serves as lieutenant in the tower of Minas Morgul.
Takes command of Mordor's army after the Witch-king falls.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book V

title: Mouth of Sauron
blurb: The Mouth of Sauron was the herald of Barad-dûr. He met the Captains of the West at the Black Gate to demand their surrender.
book:
The Mouth of Sauron was a Black Númenórean who served Sauron for a very long time. He forgot his own name and became the Lieutenant of Barad-dûr.

In T.A. 3019 he rode to the Black Gate to meet the Captains of the West. He showed them Sam's sword, an Elven cloak with its brooch, and Frodo's mithril coat to suggest that Frodo was captured. He demanded terms of surrender.

Gandalf took the tokens and refused. The Mouth then turned back in fear, and the battle began.
film: In the extended edition he is played by Bruce Spence. Aragorn cuts off his head at the Black Gate.

places.note: Serves Sauron as his Lieutenant in the Dark Tower.
Meets the Captains at the Black Gate and demands their surrender.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book V

title: Elendil
kind: High King of Arnor and Gondor
blurb: Elendil was a Númenórean who escaped the Downfall, founded Arnor and Gondor, and died fighting Sauron in the Last Alliance.
book:
Elendil was a lord of the Faithful of Númenor. He was called the Tall. He was the son of Amandil and the father of Isildur and Anárion.

When Númenor was drowned in S.A. 3319, he escaped with nine ships and reached Middle-earth. He founded the realms of Arnor and Gondor in exile and was High King. He made his home at Annúminas and set a palantír in the tower of Elostirion.

In S.A. 3434 he joined Gil-galad in the Last Alliance of Elves and Men. They defeated Sauron's host on Dagorlad and besieged Barad-dûr.

In S.A. 3441 Sauron came out to fight on the slopes of Mount Doom and killed both Elendil and Gil-galad. Elendil's sword Narsil broke beneath him. His son Isildur took up the hilt-shard. Isildur later made a tomb for Elendil on the hill that the Rohirrim call Halifirien.
film: Elendil's death at the hands of Sauron is shown in the prologue to the first film.

facts.Title: High King of Arnor and Gondor

places.note: Lands in Lindon after the Downfall and is welcomed by Gil-galad.
Makes Annúminas the royal seat of Arnor.
Sets a palantír in this tower to look west over the sea.
Helps destroy Sauron's host in the Last Alliance.
Falls in combat with Sauron on the slopes of Mount Doom.
Isildur makes his tomb on the summit of Halifirien.

sources: The Silmarillion
The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A

title: Isildur
kind: Son of Elendil, King of Gondor and Arnor
blurb: Isildur cut the Ring from Sauron's hand but kept it. Orcs killed him at the Gladden Fields in T.A. 2.
book:
Isildur was the elder son of Elendil. He escaped the Downfall of Númenor and founded Minas Ithil. He planted a seedling of the White Tree in the city.

In the Last Alliance he fought at Dagorlad and in the siege of Barad-dûr. When Sauron killed Elendil, Isildur used his father's broken sword to cut the Ring from Sauron's hand. Sauron's body perished.

Isildur refused to destroy the Ring at Mount Doom. He kept it, and the Ring corrupted him.

In T.A. 2 Orcs attacked his company at the Gladden Fields. Isildur put on the Ring and escaped into the river, but the Ring slipped from his finger. Orc arrows killed him. The Ring was lost in the water.
film: Harry Sinclair plays Isildur. The film shows him refusing to destroy the Ring in the fire of Mount Doom.

places.note: Founds Minas Ithil (later Minas Morgul) and plants the White Tree.
Fights in the great battle against Sauron.
Cuts the Ring from Sauron's hand on the slopes of Mount Doom and keeps it.
Is killed by Orcs, and the Ring is lost.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book II
The Silmarillion
Unfinished Tales

title: Anárion
kind: Son of Elendil, co-founder of Gondor
blurb: Anárion was the younger son of Elendil. He ruled Gondor with Isildur and died at the siege of Barad-dûr.
book:
Anárion was the younger son of Elendil. He escaped the Downfall of Númenor and founded Minas Anor in the southern realm. He and Isildur ruled Gondor together.

He held Osgiliath against Sauron, who attacked Ithilien. In the Last Alliance he fought in the siege of Barad-dûr. In S.A. 3440 a stone thrown from the tower killed him.

His son Meneldil later ruled Gondor. All the kings of Gondor descended from Anárion.
film: Anárion does not appear in the films.

places.note: Founds Minas Anor, later called Minas Tirith.
Rules from Osgiliath with his brother.
Is slain by a stone cast from Barad-dûr during the siege.

sources: The Silmarillion
The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A

title: Elendur
blurb: Elendur was the eldest son of Isildur and his heir. He fell beside his father at the Gladden Fields in T.A. 2.
book:
Elendur was the eldest son of Isildur. He went with his father when Isildur marched north to Arnor after the war.

Orcs ambushed their company at the Gladden Fields in T.A. 2. Elendur was killed in the fight, as were his brothers Aratan and Ciryon. His father also died.

Only his youngest brother Valandil, who was safe at Rivendell, remained to take the crown of Arnor.
film: Elendur does not appear in the films.

places.note: Is killed beside his father in the Orc ambush.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A
Unfinished Tales

title: Valandil
blurb: Valandil was the youngest son of Isildur. He survived the Gladden Fields and became the third King of Arnor.
book:
Valandil was the youngest son of Isildur. He was left in Rivendell while his father marched north, so he escaped the ambush at the Gladden Fields.

After Isildur and his elder sons fell, Valandil became King of Arnor in T.A. 10. He ruled from Annúminas and was the third king, after Elendil and Isildur.

He reigned until his death in T.A. 249. His descendants ruled Arnor and its successor kingdoms, and from them came the Chieftains of the Dúnedain.
film: Valandil does not appear in the films.

places.note: Is kept in Rivendell when his father marches north.
Rules Arnor from Annúminas.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A

title: Meneldil
kind: Third King of Gondor, son of Anárion
blurb: Meneldil was the son of Anárion. He ruled Gondor after Isildur went north and began its long line of kings.
book:
Meneldil was the son of Anárion. Before Isildur marched north, he gave Meneldil the rule of Gondor. After Isildur died, Meneldil ruled Gondor alone.

He ruled for many years from Osgiliath, the chief city of the realm, and kept the realm as his father had left it.

All later kings of Gondor came from him. His descendants held the throne until the line ended with Eärnur.
film: Meneldil does not appear in the films.

places.note: Rules Gondor from Osgiliath after the Last Alliance.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A
